$comment-tag-format: include-component-in-tag MUST stay false, and it is the setting most likely to be dropped when copying this file, because nothing about it looks load-bearing. With it absent release-please defaults to true and names the tag `nestor-meaning-v0.4.0` instead of `v0.4.0`. publish.yml triggers on `v*`, which that does not match -- so the tag would be created and nothing would publish, with no error anywhere. That exact mistake was made on willow-mcp#256. tests/test_version.py checks the produced tag against the workflow trigger, because a comment did not stop it happening once.
$comment-no-extra-files: There is deliberately no `extra-files` block. The version is tag-derived (hatch-vcs, see pyproject [tool.hatch.version]), so nothing in the tree holds a version string for release-please to bump -- which is the same reason kartikeya has none and willow-mcp does (its .claude-plugin/plugin.json carries its own copy, and that copy drifted to 2.0.0 while the package was 2.0.1). Adding a file here would be reintroducing the second source of truth that this repo just removed.
$comment-first-bump: bump-minor-pre-major false means a breaking change goes to 1.0.0 rather than being held at a minor, and bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major false keeps `fix:` at a patch. This repo is past 0.3.1 with a published PyPI history, so the pre-1.0 caution those flags exist for buys nothing here: a break should say 1.0.0. WHAT IS NOT GUARANTEED: this keys off the commit type, so a breaking change mislabelled `refactor:` still ships as a patch. Nothing in this file can catch that -- the pr-title.yml gate covers the other direction (a title claiming a release its commits do not).
